verified: Guideline adjudication of the prior encoding finding. The div keeps the reusable canonical identity chol/shacharit/torah/gaddelu. The prayer-part milestone carries a local occurrence URN, rosh_hashanah/torah/gaddelu/text. The bounded seg carries source=bible:psalms/34/4 with local chapter/verse quotation milestones and terminators. None of the quoted guidelines requires every milestone URN inside a div to sit beneath the div's URN. The URN-scope rules (1-4) define scope by milestone position and unit, not by URN hierarchy. 'Do not duplicate a canonical URN merely because the text is printed again elsewhere' is respected, because the local URN is not a second copy of a canonical one. 'A tei:seg remains appropriate for a bounded quotation carrying source … place its milestone before the semantic span' is followed. I found no violation of the actual guidelines, so the prior encoding objection is withdrawn.

The registry convention exists. siddur.jsonl contains many status=context entries with rosh_hashanah occurrence parents and 'canonical identity reused' notes (for example lines 2541-2591, 2769-2777). In the portions I read, I did not reach the specific rosh_hashanah/torah/gaddelu/text entry, so I record its presence as the user's statement and do not independently confirm it (see limits).
HE and EN carry identical corresp sets (local text, quotation chapter/verse), so they align.

Prior unresolved citation question resolved from the code. opensiddur/common/subverse.py VERSE_PARTS declares ('numbers', 9, 23): (('al_pi', {'he': 'על פי יהוה ביד משה'}),), commented 'The scroll-lifting formula appends only the closing words of this verse.'

_incipit_offset matches the whole five-word consonantal incipit at a token start. Numbers 9:23 has several על־פי phrases. The first is followed by יחנו. The second begins ועל (consonants ועל ≠ על) and is followed by יסעו. Only the final על־פי יהוה ביד משה matches the full declared phrase, so the part starts at the closing words. The previous reader's 'fourth occurrence' count was wrong, but the conclusion is unaffected: the declared phrase is unique in the verse.

The scope of verse-part al_pi runs to the end of verse 23, which is exactly the quoted closing words, so bible:numbers/9/23/al_pi denotes the printed text. In both HE and EN, the local verse-part milestone n=al_pi is closed by a bare verse-part terminator, then verse, then chapter, as the sub-verse terminator rules require.

s164-row5 line 2 rechecked: אֶחָד אֱלֹהֵינוּ גָּדוֹל אֲדוֹנֵנוּ קָדוֹשׁ (וְנוֹרָא) שְׁמוֹ: The parenthesis is printed, and no rubric, siglum or occasion is printed with it anywhere on the row.

Guideline adjudication. Conditional text says added-or-omitted text is a condition, and @type="marked" describes how an undecided scope the source brackets is set off. But a j:conditional needs a feature structure that says when the words apply, and the source gives no occasion. Supplying a specific condition would be invention. The guidelines do not require a j:conditional where no condition can be stated from the source, and j:option does not fit, because there is no second wording.

Keeping the printed parenthesis inline is consistent with how the independently accepted (הוּא) in uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah was handled (review 01). An anonymous reader-option marked conditional would only be appropriate if a registered feature for such an option already exists, and I found none cited in the guideline excerpts. So the current literal encoding is accepted and the prior encoding objection is withdrawn.

Calendar logic. The source says: omit on day 2, except when day 1 fell on Shabbat. Encoded: any( rosh-hashana=1 , all( rosh-hashana=2 , hebrew-day=1 ) ). If day 1 is Shabbat, day 2 is Sunday, and per the stated convention hebrew-day=1 is Sunday, so the logic is exactly equivalent. Rosh Hashanah day 1 never falls on Sunday, so the Sunday test cannot misfire for a day-1 Shabbat case. The single j:all wrapping one j:any is redundant but harmless.

The condition is consistent with the enclosing running-order gate documentary_shofar_weekday_he (shabbat=false, review.xml line 600): on a day-1 Shabbat the whole shofar section is excluded, and on day 2 (Sunday) it is included.
